title: Mission
description: A single short mission, 12-20 minutes. Missions are declarative data, never TypeScript. If a mission needs behaviour this schema cannot express, extend the schema rather than writing engine code -- that is what keeps missions authorable by contributors who do not know the codebase.

phase.description: The phase this mission is built around. One lead phase per mission.

ledger.description: The campaign carry-over contract. This is what lets a contributor author one mission without reading the whole campaign.

requires.description: Ledger keys read on entry. Missing or sparse values must degrade gracefully into a harder mission, never a broken one.

items.description: Player deployment. Deliberately NOT the shared placement $def, and deliberately without `in_tunnel`: the runtime would accept a buried player unit, but nothing player-side can dig a route open, every command to a buried body is refused, and its living corpse would hold off the wipe-loss check -- an unlosable, unplayable start. additionalProperties:false is the gate that keeps that state unauthorable; validate_data.mjs refuses the same key on reinforce triggers, the other player-side spawn path.

from_ledger.description: If true, draw survivors with veterancy from roster.surviving_units instead of spawning fresh.

supply_corridor.description: If true, logistics income can be interdicted by the enemy. Protecting the corridor becomes gameplay.

type.description: destroy_all exists but should be rare. Layered objectives are what make a level a level. raze: every structure inside the zone named by `target` is destroyed. The set is snapshotted at mission start, so a zone holding no structures is an authoring error rather than an instant win. collapse: every tunnel route whose MOUTH lies inside the zone named by `target` is brought down; a route that merely passes under the zone does not count. The set is snapshotted at mission start, so a zone holding no mouths can never complete and is an authoring error. A primary collapse must declare `seconds`, for the same reason a primary raze must: losing every unit that can work a charge makes it permanently impossible, and without a deadline to fail on the mission is unwinnable and unlosable at once.

unlocks_phase.description: Gate: assault cannot begin until civilians are clear, etc.

roe.description: Rules of engagement scoring. Must be visible in the HUD at all times -- the player should always know what a shot costs before taking it.

flagged_zones.description: Map zone ids under protection (clinic, mosque, school). Player ordnance landing inside deducts flagged_structure_penalty per impact.

fail_below.description: Mission failure threshold. Omit for no hard fail.

structure_penalty_mult.description: Scales each destroyed building's roe_penalty. 0 disables structure scoring for missions where the town is already rubble.

civilians.description: Non-combatants in the area of operations. Untargetable by either side; hurt only by ordnance. They shelter in place until fire lands close, then flee to the refuge.

refuge.description: Marker civilians run to once spooked.

garrison.description: Defenders emplaced at mission start, with the GDD §6 behaviour vocabulary: one stance per unit, declarative, never scripted.

trigger.description: Optional objective id; wave fires on completion instead of on the clock.

to.description: Marker the wave attack-moves toward after spawning. Defaults to holding at the spawn.

from.description: Spawn point or tunnel id. Tunnels keep producing until located and collapsed.

triggers.description: Reactive behaviour (GDD §6): a condition fires an order once. A handful per mission is the budget.

zone.description: zone_entered: map zone id a player unit must enter.

group.description: commit/withdraw_to: which garrison group moves. dismount: whose carriers unload.

units.description: spawn: enemy units. reinforce: player units.

structures.description: Buildings this mission raises, on top of whatever its map already has. The map's character grid is shared between every mission that names it, so a structure only one mission should own -- a field camp -- belongs here rather than in the grid. Raised by MissionRuntime.start(), which is the one path every loader already goes through.

marker.description: Spawn at a named map marker instead of coordinates.

in_tunnel.description: Route id (map tunnels[].id) this placement starts inside. The bodies spawn underground in that route rather than standing on their tile, and stay below until the route is dug through and vents -- or die with it if it is collapsed first. Enemy and civilian placements only; player-side burial is refused (see starting_force). Mutually exclusive with a garrison stance, a tag, passengers, and digs, and the route must exist on the mission's map -- all enforced by validate_data.mjs, which also rejects a burial in a route this mission leaves unopenable: the route must be pre_dug, or dug by a digs placement in the same mission, or the garrison could never surface.

digs.description: Route id (map tunnels[].id) whose digger this placement is: the spawned body is assigned to the route at mission start and the dig advances from the first tick -- the declarative form of digger assignment, exactly as in_tunnel is of stocking a route. One digger, one route: the unit must carry the dig_tunnel ability, count must be 1, no two placements may dig the same route, a pre_dug route is refused (nothing left to excavate), and a placement cannot be in_tunnel and dig at once -- all enforced by validate_data.mjs, which also rejects a digs naming a route the map does not declare; the runtime throws on the same unknown id before any body spawns.

passengers.description: Infantry authored aboard this carrier, seated at spawn rather than walking in. The only way an AI-driven transport ever has passengers -- every other route is a player command. Each carrier in a count>1 placement gets the whole declared load, not a share of it. Capacity and whether a type can ride are checked by validate_data.mjs, which unlike this schema can see the carrier's transport_slots. Note `starting_force` carries its own inline copy of this object and does not accept this field; nothing player-side needs it yet.

tiles.description: ambush: hold fire and minimum signature until a target closes to this range.

building.description: garrison: tile coordinates of any tile of the building to occupy. The unit spawns outside and moves in.
